name: Hydrogen water / topical hydrogen

lead: Hydrogen water and hydrogen skincare are marketed as antioxidant anti-ageing products.
Reference sources describe clinical evidence for hydrogen therapy as limited, and none specific to appearance was located.

paras: Proponents say dissolved H2 reduces oxidative stress and inflammation; this is a proposed mechanism with preliminary support.
Safety information was not found in the sources reviewed. Evidence of benefit is limited.

lead: Hydrogen water and topical hydrogen products are drinks and skincare items infused with molecular hydrogen (H2), promoted in some wellness and anti-ageing circles for antioxidant effects on skin and the body.

Wikipedia's article on hydrogen therapy states that its efficacy has not been established, that proposed benefits are linked to reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, and that large-scale clinical evidence is limited.[1] That article does not address hydrogen water products, safety or skin claims specifically.

paras: Proponents describe molecular hydrogen as a selective antioxidant and promote it either dissolved in drinking water or applied through skincare. The proposed appearance benefit is slower skin ageing via reduced oxidative stress.

Reviewed research on hydrogen therapy is described as preliminary. Proposed areas include neurological disorders, spinal cord injury, liver protection and cardiometabolic health, each with limited or emerging clinical evidence, and optimal dosing and targets are said to be unclear.[1] Research on age-related disease is ongoing with clinical evidence described as limited.[1]
No studies found on hydrogen water or topical hydrogen for facial appearance. Studies of hydrogen therapy in general, for non-cosmetic conditions, are described as limited.[1]
